pages.text: "Yahooooo!" Pongi shouted as loudly as she could on the bank path under the bridge. The sound echoed and grew louder. The swallows in their nests under the bridge all fluttered away.
"Wow! My voice gets bigger! Again!" Pongi shouted again. Dad, in his overalls, flinched and hunched his shoulders beside her. "Pongi, that's too loud! My ears hurt..."
The swallows had flown far away above the reeds. Under the bridge were only seven empty nests. Left alone, Pongi murmured, "Oh... why did all the swallows leave?"

Dad looked up at the empty nests. "Under the bridge, your voice echoes and gets louder. When you shout, the swallows get a fright and fly away." Pongi shut her mouth and stayed still. "Really? I didn't know..."
Dad explained, "Whisper under the bridge, and speak loudly on the wide bank!" Pongi looked up beneath the bridge. "Under the bridge, whisper softly!" she repeated in a little voice.
"Let's play whispering," Dad said very quietly. "Under the bridge, only this loud..." Pongi copied him in a whisper. "Like this?" Then one swallow quietly came back to its nest.
This time they stood on the wide bank. "You can shout here!" said Dad. Pongi stretched both paws up and called, "Yahooooo!" She thumped her tail on the bank.

From the bridge, Grandpa Goose, the canal keeper in boots, looked down. "All the swallows are back." Seven swallows sat in a row in the nests below. Pongi whispered, "Under the bridge, whisper softly!"

It was evening. Dad slept on the sofa. Pongi whispered, "One, whisper under the bridge! Two, speak loudly on the bank! Three, lower your voice if someone gets a fright!" "Shh. Dad is sleeping." She tiptoed.

Dad opened his eyes and gave Pongi a snug hug. "Thanks to you, I slept well." With a voice that fits the place, neither the swallows nor Dad get a fright. Pongi whispered, "Under the bridge, whisper softly!"
